sources.excerpt: Okko FX Diablo Dual Overdrive | Delicious Audio Creative Pedals Creative Delay Tape Delay W/ Reverb Delay Distortion Fuzz Overdrive Dual Gain Dirt Boost Compr. + Dynamics Dynamics EQ Filter Wah Filter+EQ Lo-Fi 8 Bit Lo-fi Chorus Flanger Phaser Tremolo Uni-Vibe Modulation Pitch Shifter Octaver pitch Multiverb Reverb Spring Reverb Reverb CV In Granular Synth Pedals Synth Effect Guides Monthly Lists Shopping Guides Coverage Schedule Facebook Stompbox Exhibit Okko FX Diablo Dual Overdrive Updated Oct. 4, 2023 | by Paolo De Gregorio The Diablo overdrive (now out of production) was one of OKKO ‘s most successful stompbox designs, featuring some novel fine-tuning controls like the Headroom switch (which ups the circuit’s headroom to 18v), the Feed knob (controlling the amount of bass in the input signal) and the Body knob (affecting mids and dynamics). The pedal’s main selling point was that it sounded great also through through clean amps – something rare for overdrives. 15 years after its first release the German manufacturer decided to offer an upgraded version of it with the Diablo Dual , which sports some features often requested by the many fans of the original device. The main difference of the Dual version is that – yes you guessed it – it features two channels. Switching duties are taken care of by the left footswitch, which, in a previous version called Diablo+ , was used for a simple extra gain boost placed on top of the OD; the Diablo Dual, instead, gives you two overdrives with separate Drive and Level knobs. The setting on the upper row knobs are shared by the two channels, and feature two new, three-way toggle switches that let you tailor the pedal to your guitar’s Input and find the best sounding Mids for your amp. Okko FX Diablo Dual Overdrive, Builder’s Notes Since the first Diablos hit the market 15 years ago they found a permanent place on thousands of pedalboards all over the world. The Dual adds some often requested features to the classic Diablo circuit. The DIABLO DUAL offers exceptional dynamic qualities and super-clear, amp-like sounds. Unlike many other overdrives it works perfectly with clean amps. What makes it so special is a set of controls that affecst the “feel” of the pedal, the way how it reacts to your playing. DYN (AMIC) adjusts the internal voltage from about 6 to 18 volts. Increasing the headroom results in less compression, tighter bass and more punch. FEED controls low frequencies in the input signal allowing tight and transparent sounds even with the fattest sounding neck pickups. BODY control is a bit different from the older Diablo (and also from the GH model). It adds bass and low mids for a fat sound and different gain structure. INPUT 3-position-miniswitch (normal/lowgain/top boost) sets the sensitivity of the input gain stage for best interaction with your guitars. MIDS changes frequencies in the tone control. Perfect for matching pedal and amp tone. Each of the two channels is adjustable in GAIN and LEVEL. You can change during playing or pre-select the channels when in bypass mode. sources.excerpt: --> OKKO FX Diablo Dual Demo Review | Loopy Demos Show or hide the side bar navigation Loopy Demos Demos Posts Manufacturers About Contact Demos Posts Manufacturers About Contact All demos OKKO FX Diablo Dual Oct 26, 2023 The OKKO FX Diablo Dual makes you smile the moment you plug in. It’s a low to mid gain overdrive handmade in Leipzig, Germany, and it sounds like your amp on a very good day: clear, chimey, dynamically alive. Guitar works beautifully with it, and so does bass. What separates this from a standard dirt box is the tonal shaping on offer. Four global knobs shape both channels at once, each channel has its own Drive and Level, and two mini toggles dial in sensitivity and midrange character. It sounds complex on paper. In practice, it just sounds right. Controls The top row runs left to right: DYN, FEED, BODY, TONE. DYN adjusts the internal voltage from roughly 6 to 18 volts. Low DYN compresses and softens the attack; high DYN opens up headroom, tightens the bass, and adds punch. It’s the most dramatic control on the pedal. FEED determines how much low-end enters the circuit. Roll it back for a leaner, cutting tone; push it and the drive gets bigger and rawer, eventually approaching fuzz-like density. BODY adjusts the lows and low-mids. TONE shapes the upper mids. Between the channel controls sit two mini toggles. The Input toggle (normal/low gain/top boost) sets the sensitivity of the input gain stage for your guitar. The Mids toggle shifts the frequency the Tone control acts on, letting you match the pedal to your amp. The lower row gives each channel its own Drive and Level: channel one on the left pair, channel two on the right. You switch between them with the footswitch. In the demo above I’ve set up sweeps for Drive, Dyn, Feed, Body, Tone, Input, and Mids so you can hear each control do its thing in isolation. How It Sounds The Diablo Dual lives between clean boost and medium gain crunch. The DYN control is voltage headroom on demand, and it’s what makes this thing feel so amp-like. Cozy Saturation sits DYN at midpoint and Feed high: compression holds everything together with warm, smooth bloom. Edge of Breakup opens DYN up and pulls Feed back, so single notes ring out clean and chords grind just enough. Crunch with Attitude pushes Drive higher and drops DYN; the compression squashes harder and the breakup gets raunchier. Articulate Fuzz drops DYN to zero while maxing Feed and Drive together, getting thick and chewy. That’s the outer limit of the circuit, not the typical use case. The two-channel setup earns its keep live. One channel as your base tone, the other as a pushed lead, or different sensitivity settings for two guitars. Diablo Dual vs Morning Glory V4 The JHS Morning Glory V4 is the natural cross-shop. Both are low-to-mid gain, amp-like overdrives that work well with a clean amp. The Morning Glory has a fixed, focused character: that slightly mid-humped Bluesbreaker voice with a bass cut and a gain toggle. What you hear is largely what you get, and that’s a strength if you know you like that voice. The Diablo Dual asks more of you but gives more back. DYN, Feed, Body, and Tone let you shape the circuit’s personality deeply, the two toggles add another layer of rig matching, and dual channels mean two distinct sounds with one footswitch. The Morning Glory wins on simplicity. The Diablo Dual wins when you want to dial something in precisely. Who It’s For This suits players who want one overdrive to cover clean boost, edge-of-breakup, and medium crunch without swapping pedals. Live use is where the dual-channel footswitch really earns its place. Bass players get a genuinely usable option too. If you want something you can set once and leave, a simpler one-knob boost will serve you better. The Diablo Dual has a learning curve.
